title: Families Denied Financial Assistance Due to Per Capital Household Income Requirement
what_it_is: Families Denied Financial Assistance Due to Per Capital Household Income Requirement

sections.label: ComCare payouts and eligibility questions
sections.summary: Questions ask whether ComCare and Public Assistance payouts can be revised, how many families received ComCare under the $650 PCHI benchmark, projected numbers at $800, and reasons for rejected assistance requests.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Social and Family Development whether the Ministry can revise the monthly ComCare Long Term Assistance or the Public Assistance Scheme payouts, as well as support for other major assistance programmes, to assist vulnerable Singaporeans in the face of rising costs of living.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Social and Family Development (a) for the past year, how many families have received ComCare support based on the previous criteria of per capita household income (PCHI) benchmark of $650 and below; (b) with the increase in the PCHI benchmark to $800 and below, what is the projected number of families that will be eligible for ComCare support; and (c) whether the Ministry can consider reaching out to the families that have missed the previous criteria but are now eligible for assistance based on the new criteria.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Social and Family Development with the rise in inflation (a) whether there has been an increase in the number of financial assistance requests received from 2020 to 2023; (b) whether the number of requests that do not qualify for financial assistance are due to the per capita household income (PCHI) criteria; and (c) if not, what are the other reasons for not qualifying for financial assistance.

sections.label: SMTA PCHI benchmark raised
sections.summary: MSF raised the SMTA per capita household income benchmark from $650 and below to $800 and below.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: Last month, the Ministry of Social and Family Development (MSF) raised the SMTA per capita household income (PCHI) benchmark from $650 and below, to $800 and below.

sections.label: SMTA applicant numbers 2019 to 2022
sections.summary: SMTA applicants rose from around 61,000 in 2019 to around 80,000 in 2020 and 82,000 in 2021, then dropped to around 75,000 in 2022.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: The number of SMTA applicants rose from around 61,000 in 2019, to around 80,000 in 2020 and 82,000 in 2021 at the height of COVID-19, before dropping to around 75,000 in 2022.

sections.label: ComCare assistance quantum increased
sections.summary: In August 2022, the quantum of assistance was increased for households on ComCare SMTA and Long-Term Assistance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: In August 2022, we increased the quantum of assistance for households on ComCare SMTA and Long-Term Assistance (LTA).

sections.label: ComCare households in 2022
sections.summary: It was noted that 75,000 Singaporean households received ComCare assistance in 2022.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: The first one is, we noted that 75,000 Singaporean households receive ComCare assistance in 2022.

sections.label: Cash assistance reviews and support measures
sections.summary: Cash assistance is reviewed regularly, taking into account Government packages such as Budget 2023 one-off support and SSO support from 4 April to 30 September 2022.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: For the cash assistance itself, we do make reviews regularly, particularly when there are peculiar instances, like these last two years of increasing inflation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: But we do take into account, first, the packages available from the Government, such as at Budget 2023 when Deputy Prime Minister Lawrence Wong announced a set of additional one-off support measures to Singaporeans to address immediate cost of living, and this included the 2023 cost-of-living special payment of up to $400 in cash to provide for this relief.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: And then on top of that, MSF also announced from 4 April to 30 September 2022, SSOs provided a minimum of six months of support.
